tier_reason: The README numbers are reproducible from the public snapshot at commit e383614 (2023-02-16): the harnesses are src/deno/bench/mod.bench.ts and src/node/bench/index.bench.ts, the Dockerfile pins rust:1.64.0, wasm/Cargo.toml sets opt-level "z" and lto, and the README names the CPU (Apple M1 Max) and the Deno and Node versions. Every row runs the named baseline, @noble/curves 0.7.x, on the same keygen+sign+verify loop.

corrections.workload: Per iteration: generate a random Ed25519 keypair, derive the public key, sign a 1 KiB random message and verify the signature. Measured with deno bench and a Node benchSync harness (1,000 samples). 'Unserialized' keeps keys as wasm objects; 'serialized' round-trips them through bytes. Rows: berith, @noble/curves 0.7.x, supercop.wasm 5.0.1 and node:crypto.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: The numbers date from February 2023; the README benchmark output is identical at commit e383614 (2023-02-16). That build used the rust:1.64.0 Docker image and wasm-pack build --target web --release (wasm-pack itself unpinned). The Cargo release profile was opt-level "z" with lto true, and the crates were ed25519-dalek 1.0.1 and x25519-dalek 1.2.0 with u64_backend. Runtimes were Deno 1.30.3 and Node v18.12.1. The baseline was @noble/curves 0.7.0 in Deno and 0.7.1 in Node (per package-lock, though the row is labelled 0.7.0). The current HEAD build (rust 1.71.0 Dockerfile, opt-level 3, ed25519-dalek 2.0.0, Sept 2023 rewrite) has never been re-benchmarked.
corrections.caveats: The repository is marked DEPRECATED in favour of @hazae41/ed25519 and @hazae41/x25519. Code last changed in October 2023, and every commit since then (to 2025-05-25) is a README edit. The README numbers were measured on the February 2023 code (dalek 1.x, size-optimised opt-level z, rust 1.64.0) and were not regenerated after the September 2023 rewrite. The current bench files have no serialized rows, and the Node bench imports @noble/curves unpinned (^1.2.0), so re-running HEAD measures different code against a different baseline. The baseline, @noble/curves 0.7.x from early 2023, is old, so the 5.85-7.06x ratio is dated. The same table shows berith slower than supercop.wasm 5.0.1 (187.96 vs 281.68 us) and slower than node:crypto unserialized (152.67 us): the win is only against pure JS. The README's summary prints slowdowns as '0.67x faster' and '0.54x faster'. Each iteration bundles key generation, signing and verification, so per-operation costs are not separated. The Unlicense is a public-domain dedication with no patent grant.

notes: The numbers match the README exactly (5.85x Deno, 7.06x Node against noble 0.7.x), with supercop.wasm and node:crypto faster than berith on the same page. The record's compiler_and_flags described the 2023-09 HEAD build, not the February 2023 build that produced the numbers; that field is corrected. The project is deprecated by its author, and the successor packages @hazae41/ed25519 and @hazae41/ed25519.wasm are not in this record. Category fit is loose: it is a Rust library compiled to wasm, not a wasm language.

tier_reason: These are first-party numbers from a public harness (benchmark/run.js and generate_samples.js) on a named CPU (Apple M4) with stated flags. The compiler that decides the generated code is not recorded, though: the table was last updated 2026-04-09 (commit 885e989), the Yo version was pinned only on 2026-10-10, and the clang, Emscripten and Node versions are not stated. The record's claim that the Yo version is pinned in .yo-version does not hold for these numbers, so this is partial methodology and the tier is C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: The numbers were last updated 2026-04-09 (commit 885e989, 'update benchmarks for -O3 optimization'). The Yo compiler version used then was not recorded; .yo-version did not exist, and the pin to Yo 0.2.58 was added on 2026-10-10. Native build: Yo Optimize.ReleaseFast to C, then clang -O3 -flto (clang version not stated; devenv.nix takes clang from nixpkgs). WASM CLI build (markdown_yo_wasm_exe): Yo Optimize.ReleaseSmall, then emcc -O3 -flto -mbulk-memory -sNODERAWFS -sEXIT_RUNTIME=1 -sALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH -sINITIAL_MEMORY=67108864 -sWASM_BIGINT (Emscripten version not stated). Baseline: markdown-it ^14.1.1 called with {html: true} on Node (devenv.nix nodejs_22; exact version not stated). The harness is benchmark/run.js.
corrections.workload: Markdown-to-HTML conversion of one synthetic ~1.2 KB block (headings, nested lists, blockquote, code fence, table, links, an image and entities, no raw HTML), repeated to 64 KB, 256 KB, 1 MB, 5 MB and 20 MB (benchmark/generate_samples.js). markdown-it is timed in-process on render() only: median of 10 runs after 3 warmups. Native and WASM are timed as the wall time of a whole child process (startup, file read, then 20 conversions with output discarded under --repeat 20) divided by 20.
corrections.caveats: The license is declared as MIT only in yo.toml and npm/package.json; the repository has no LICENSE file. The benchmark input is one synthetic block repeated many times, not real documents. The table dates from 2026-04-09 and the code has gone through many Yo language migrations since, so it has not been re-measured on the current code. The harness does not compare outputs between implementations; CommonMark conformance (815/826 spec tests) is checked separately. markdown-it runs with html: true while markdown_yo runs without --html; the samples contain no raw HTML, so this is probably immaterial. The WASM rows divide whole-process time, including Node startup and wasm compilation, by 20. At 64 KB that is about 0.26 s per process (12.9 ms x 20, derived from page data), and WASM is slower than markdown-it below about 1 MB (0.1x at 64 KB, 0.5x at 256 KB). Single-shot use is far slower than the table suggests. The in-process wasm_api build shipped in the npm package is not benchmarked. The project started 2026-04-01 and checks in AI-assistant planning files (AGENTS.md, PLAN.md); it has a single author and is pre-1.0 (0.0.16).

notes: The numbers match the README table exactly; the native build is 4.5-7.6x faster than markdown-it and WASM is 2.1-6.0x faster only at 1 MB and above. Downgraded from A to C because the Yo compiler version, along with clang, Emscripten and Node, was not recorded when the April 2026 numbers were taken, and the code has changed substantially since. The harness is otherwise reasonable and, if anything, conservative toward markdown_yo, since process startup is included on its side only. The record's 'one month old' was wrong: the first commit is 2026-04-01.

tier_reason: The harnesses are public: benches/wasm/bench.mjs (Node 64-leaf batch), pda.mjs and browser/browser-bench.mjs (Chrome grind). They run @noble/hashes, the stated baseline, with a correctness gate against node:crypto. The build command and flags (RUSTFLAGS +simd128, cargo build --release --example wasm_lib) and the CPU (Apple M4 Max) are stated. The rustc version is not stated, but the crate sets rust-version 1.89 and commits Cargo.lock.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+simd128' cargo build --release --example wasm_lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown. The rustc version is not stated (Cargo.toml rust-version 1.89; Cargo.lock committed). Runtimes: Node v24 (V8, 'unpinned, read as ratios') and Chrome 150. JS baselines: @noble/hashes ^1.5.0 and hash-wasm ^4.11.0 (benches/wasm/package.json). Harnesses: bench.mjs, pda.mjs, matrix.cjs and browser/browser-bench.mjs in benches/wasm. Estimator: best of 15 rounds x 50 iterations after 200 warmups.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1 star, 0 forks, 13 commits (July-August 2026); crate tape-sha256 0.2.1 on crates.io, 468 downloads
corrections.caveats: Inside Node, native node:crypto is much faster than this wasm build: crypto.hash one-shot takes 42.89 us per batch against 100.61 us for tape wasm (2.3x, derived from page data). The author recommends a napi binding over wasm in Node. In a browser, WebCrypto beats the wasm build on batched ~1 KB messages (75 us vs 80-90 us), and the page recommends WebCrypto there. So the win is against pure-JS noble and against hash-wasm, mainly for small messages in synchronous loops. For PDA derivation the gain is only 4%, because the ed25519 curve check dominates. Chrome clamps performance.now to 100 us, so the batch rows are quantised to 5 us steps. Node is unpinned, and the noble baseline is the 1.x line used by @solana/web3.js 1.x, not the latest noble. The repository is very young, has a single author and one star.

notes: The numbers match benches/wasm/README.md. Node 64-leaf batch: 100.61 vs 337.97 us against noble (3.36x, derived) and against 156.24 us for hash-wasm (1.55x, derived). Chrome grind: 4.55 M/s, 3.72x noble and 1.61x hash-wasm. The record omitted that node:crypto (42.89 us) beats the wasm in Node; that is now in the caveats. The crate's native SIMD claims against sha2, Firedancer and isa-l in BENCHMARKS.md could be a lead for a hashing category.
